channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies found that ACLR patients exhibited lower peak knee flexion angle, adduction angle, and flexion moment during walking compared to controls. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) was associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, while early surgery (within 6 months) showed fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but temporary frontal-plane asymmetries.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found that manual physiotherapy techniques demonstrated a large, statistically significant pooled effect (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001) in improving cervical range of motion in infants with congenital muscular torticollis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: A 6-month prospective cohort study of 112 stroke patients found that stride time variability (STV) at discharge was an independent predictor of post-discharge falls. Fallers had significantly higher STV, and an optimal STV cutoff of 3.40% (AUC 0.756) showed high sensitivity (88.2%) in identifying fall risk.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Selective distal upper extremity recovery following targeted dentate nucleus temporal interference stimulation in stroke-double-blind, sham-controlled randomized controlled trial with resting-state EEG
item.description: A double-blind, sham-controlled RCT (N=47) showed that 10 sessions of dentate nucleus-targeted tTIS combined with rehabilitation significantly improved FMA-UE (adjusted mean difference 3.98 points, p = 0.006) and ARAT (adjusted mean difference 2.98 points, p = 0.005) in subacute stroke patients, particularly for distal motor control (d=2.46, p<0.001), compared to sham.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine RCTs (n=348) found action observation therapy significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.53 to 1.19), activities of daily living (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.22 to 1.12), and naming aphasia (SMD = 0.53, 95% CI = 0.01 to 1.05) in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Network-Based Brain Stimulation: Targeting the Frontoparietal Network for Cognitive Rehabilitation After Stroke Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found that non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) targeting the frontoparietal network significantly improved executive function (Hedges' g = 0.48), working memory (g = 0.41), and attention (g = 0.38) in stroke survivors, with superior outcomes when combined with cognitive training.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
item.description: A randomized crossover trial found that virtual reality (VR) and screen-based augmented reality (AR) feedback during robot-assisted gait training acutely and differentially modulated paretic muscle activation, limb loading, and propulsion-related mechanics in chronic hemiparetic stroke, with sequential combined VR + AR producing the broadest acute modulation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials found that low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome, with pulsed mode superior for analgesia and continuous mode for grip strength, and improved SNCV (Hedges' g=0.377, P=0.016).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Different Neuromuscular Training Modalities and Doses on Lower-Limb Injury Prevention in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (27,663 participants) found NMT was associated with reduced lower-limb injury risk (RR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.64–0.82), with structured and multidimensional programs showing favorable pooled estimates. However, overall certainty of evidence was very low, and dose-related findings were exploratory.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated walking cost in cerebral palsy
item.description: In children with cerebral palsy (CP, N=23) and typically developing peers (TD, N=10), body-weight support significantly reduced net energetic walking cost, with a 3.5-fold greater effect in the CP group, reducing their cost by 41% to TD levels. Mediolateral stabilization had negligible energetic effects.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Venous flow dynamics in post-stroke hemiparetic lower extremity motor dysfunctions.
item.description: A retrospective cross-sectional study (n=43) in Türkiye found significantly reduced venous pump capacity (1.07 ± 0.43% vs. 2.24 ± 0.74%) and venous refilling time (9.26 ± 3.42 vs. 19.4 seconds) in post-stroke hemiparetic limbs compared to unaffected sides, with interlimb venous refilling time asymmetry correlating with Brunnstrom stage (ρ = -0.35, p = 0.022) and Barthel Index (ρ = -0.38, p = 0.012).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiological responses during high intensity interval training and moderate intensity continuous training in patients attending early cardiac rehabilitation.
item.description: In early outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) significantly increased mean VO₂, %VO₂R, time >90% VO₂R, %HRR, RPP, and blood lactate (all P < 0.003) compared to time-matched moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) in 18 coronary artery disease patients, also eliciting higher perceived exertion (RPE 13 ± 1 vs. 11 ± 1; P < 0.003).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From "Tech Fear" to Digital Self-Efficacy: A COM-B and TDF Analysis of Tele-Exercise Engagement in Older Adults at Risk of Falls
item.description: A qualitative study (n=25), nested within an RCT, explored older adults' experiences with synchronous tele-exercise for fall risk, finding successful engagement despite initial digital literacy barriers. Targeted behavior change techniques (e.g., in-home onboarding, graded tasks) fostered digital self-efficacy, making tele-exercise feasible and acceptable, challenging assumptions that low digital literacy precludes digital health adoption.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Inertial measurement unit-based gait analysis for objective assessment of vestibular rehabilitation.
item.description: A study of 30 AVS patients found that IMU-based gait analysis during T25FW tests captured significant improvements in walking speed, Gait Profile Score, and cadence after a 6-week rehabilitation program and at 12-week follow-up. Improvements were observed even with a single pelvis sensor, supporting the clinical feasibility of wearable IMU systems.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapy and Exercise-Based Rehabilitation for Mental Health: A Two-Decade Bibliometric Analysis of Global Trends, Thematic Evolution, and the Socioeconomic Vulnerability Gap (2006-2025).
item.description: A bibliometric analysis of 5223 publications from 2006-2025 revealed a 22.6-fold increase in research on physical rehabilitation and mental health, predominantly from high-income countries (75.9%). Socioeconomic vulnerability was explicitly referenced in only 4.6% of publications, indicating it as an emergent but under-researched thematic cluster.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound-Informed Hybrid Joint-Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non-Randomized Proof-of-Concept Study.
item.description: A 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid joint-sparing rehabilitation protocol was feasible and safe in 60 patients with rheumatoid arthritis, showing greater pain reduction (ΔVAS: -2.88 cm vs. -0.60 cm; p < 0.001) than a control group, though the effect size might be overestimated and ultrasonographic synovitis did not differ.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Aerobic and aerobic–cognitive training in knee osteoarthritis following acute exercise intensity selection: a two-phase randomised controlled trial protocol
item.description: This two-phase randomized controlled trial protocol will investigate aerobic and aerobic-cognitive training in knee osteoarthritis, aiming to select optimal exercise intensity (55%, 65%, or 75% HRR) based on acute sensory and hemodynamic responses (N=60 in Phase I) and evaluate their efficacy against physical-agent therapy (N=108 in Phase II) on pain (primary outcome: NRS at 12 weeks).
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: A systematic review of robotic hip exoskeletons for gait rehabilitation: from design to clinical evidence
item.description: A systematic review of 19 human subject studies (2015-2025) on robotic hip exoskeletons for gait rehabilitation found reported improvements in walking speed, step length, and symmetry across populations, with some studies showing reductions in metabolic cost and improved functional mobility. However, evidence for sustained clinical impact remains limited.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Comparison of Radiofrequency Microtenotomy vs. Heavy-Slow Resistance for Refractory Plantar Fasciopathy: A Randomised Controlled Trial
item.description: A randomized controlled superiority trial (N=72) comparing radiofrequency microtenotomy vs. heavy-slow resistance training for refractory plantar fasciopathy found no statistically significant between-group difference in FHSQ-DK pain change from baseline to 6 months (mean difference −4.9, 95% CI −13.8 to 4.0).
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: 3D Biomechanics of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries in Football: What We Have Learned in the Last Five Years.
item.description: This review synthesizes over five years of research on 3D biomechanics of ACL injuries in elite male football players, identifying a sequence of multiplanar knee rotations and marked inter-individual variability in whole-body kinematics, proposing biomechanically informed injury mitigation strategies.
item.author: PubMed
